rationale: Measure the configuration-change proposal gate that the earlier refutation rested on. A leader accepts an AddNode for node 4, and a second AddNode proposed before the first is committed or applied is replaced by an empty application entry and reported dropped under its own key. Local construction runs showed one configuration-change entry saved for the first proposal, none for the second, one application entry in its place and one dropped entry keyed 9002.

scope.description: Proposal gate at a live leader. A leader for voters {1,2,3} proposes an AddNode for node 4 and then, without committing or applying it, proposes an AddNode for node 5; the saved entries and the dropped-entry reports of both updates are recorded.
assumptions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 is leader with a committed current-term no-op; each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.

Both configuration changes are submitted through Peer.ProposeConfigChange, which enters the leader's proposal handler; no follower acknowledgement is delivered, so the first proposal stays uncommitted and unapplied.
The leader's update is inspected directly, so saved entry types and the dropped-entry report are the measured endpoints.
The surrounding node would apply a committed configuration change through ApplyConfigChange, which is not reached here.
excluded: The case does not commit or apply either change, so it measures the proposal gate only.
No transport, persistence or restart path is exercised.
The leadership-recovery check and the election gate are covered by source only.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. It proposes an AddNode config change for node 4 with key 9001 through the leader peer and records the update: how many configuration-change entries were saved and how many entries were reported dropped. Without delivering any acknowledgement it then proposes an AddNode config change for node 5 with key 9002 and records the same fields plus the key of any dropped entry and how many plain application entries were saved in place of the configuration change.
experiment.requirement: While a configuration change is pending, the leader must not append a second configuration-change entry that could later be committed with the same quorum; a second proposal must be reported dropped and must not become a configuration-change entry.
experiment.responsibility: handleLeaderPropose inspects each proposed entry, replaces a configuration change with an empty application entry and reports it dropped when the pending flag is set. The experiment exercises that handler through the real leader peer and changes only whether the first change has been applied.

comparisons.description: The first proposal must be saved as a configuration-change entry.
The second proposal must not be saved as a configuration-change entry while the first is pending.
The second proposal must be reported dropped under its own key.
